primary_intent: Create and successfully save a single Triage encounter for patient p1 containing the exact note "End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note," with no other changes. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the encounter actually being saved (committed); UI paths or minor presentation details are flexible.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the correct app, opened patient p1, set Type to Triage, and entered the exact note, making no extra changes. Critical issues: The encounter was not saved; the app returned an HTTP 401, so the primary deliverable (a committed encounter) is missing. Critical-Point rule: With permission granted, the applicable rule is FAILURE due to an environment blocker preventing completion of the binding action (the save returned 401), so the CP was not successfully crossed. Evidence: The screenshot shows 'Encounter for patient p1' with Type=Triage and the exact note text, plus a red banner 'Save failed (error 401)'; the agent’s output accurately reported this. Despite correct setup and a single save attempt, the outcome (a saved record) was not achieved, which a user would not accept.

items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: All actions occurred on http://clinic.example within the clinic's record app. The agent did not switch platforms and reported a platform error (HTTP 401) when attempting to save.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The Save button was clicked exactly once, but the server returned HTTP 401 (permission/auth error). The agent clearly reported the failure in the final output, which is an uncontrollable platform blocker.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest and only): Red banner states 'Save failed (error 401).' Save button visible. Action history shows a single Save click.
items.post_image_justification: A single save attempt was made, but the server returned HTTP 401. The agent’s final output clearly reported the failure, qualifying for full credit under uncontrollable blockers.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: Only the encounter Type and Note fields were edited and a single save attempt was made. No other fields or records were modified.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 (latest and only): Only 'Type' and 'Note' fields are edited; no other fields show changes. Save failed so no extraneous changes were persisted.

No other fields were modified, no duplicate saves were attempted, and no other records or side effects were created. Therefore, there are no unpenalized, controllable, extraneous side effects to address.
